services.title: Guest Services

overview.title: Technology for national-scale operations
overview.body1: EBI Resources' IT & Technology practice delivers enterprise software, AI platforms, cybersecurity systems, and digital workforce platforms shaped for the demands of national-scale operations.
overview.body2: The work spans five capability areas — from industrial control and cyber defense to sovereign AI, permissioned blockchain, and group-wide data fabric — presented here as a clear map for partners and technology clients.

capabilities.title: What we build
capabilities.intro: Five capability areas define the practice. Descriptions below follow the group's approved positioning — without invented case studies or metrics.

controlSystems.title: Integrated Automatic Control Systems
controlSystems.body: Sovereign control-system stack for industrial and critical infrastructure — SCADA, DCS, and ICS platforms hardened to national-grade specifications.

cybersecurity.title: Cybersecurity
cybersecurity.body: Defensive and offensive cyber capability — threat detection, incident response, red-team services, and sovereign cryptography for national-priority systems.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence
ai.body: Sovereign AI models, agentic automation, and computer-vision platforms — built for Indonesian language, regulation, and strategic-data residency.

blockchain.title: Blockchain Technology
blockchain.body: Permissioned-chain platforms for supply-chain provenance, settlement, and digital-asset issuance — tied to the group's supply-chain and trade flows.

dataIntegration.title: Data Integration
dataIntegration.body: End-to-end data fabric — ingest, lineage, and warehouse infrastructure unifying every EBI Resources subsidiary into one analytic and operational source of truth.

applications.body: Named industries, deployment contexts, and application narratives will be published once the client confirms them. Until then, we do not invent sector lists or project claims.

raja-muda-perlis-swan-x-2026.title: A visit for SWAN X 2026
raja-muda-perlis-swan-x-2026.excerpt: The Raja Muda of Perlis and a Malaysian delegation stayed at HADITH Hotel during their visit to Samarkand for SWAN X 2026.
raja-muda-perlis-swan-x-2026.alt: Members of the Perlis delegation gathered at HADITH Hotel in Samarkand.
galleryAlt: Members of the Perlis delegation presenting a Visit Perlis banner at HADITH Hotel.
The Perlis delegation and conference guests gathered in the lobby at HADITH Hotel.
body: Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, the Raja Muda of Perlis, and members of the Perlis delegation stayed at HADITH Hotel during their visit to Samarkand.

Their visit coincided with the 10th International Conference on the Prophetic Heritage (SWAN X 2026), officially opened by the Raja Muda of Perlis. The conference explores the Prophetic legacy as a guide for leadership through global instability.

HADITH Hotel was honored to welcome the delegation. Their stay brought together Malaysian guests and Samarkand hospitality during an international gathering focused on shared heritage and contemporary challenges.

turkiye-chess-teams-samarkand-olympiad.title: Türkiye’s Chess Teams Finish Strong at the Samarkand Olympiad
turkiye-chess-teams-samarkand-olympiad.excerpt: Türkiye’s Open and Women’s teams secured top-15 finishes at the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.
turkiye-chess-teams-samarkand-olympiad.alt: Türkiye’s Open and Women’s chess teams pose on the grand staircase at the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.
body: The 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad concluded in Samarkand on 27 September 2026, after 11 rounds of competition among national teams from around the world.

Türkiye finished 13th in the Open section with 15 match points and 11th in the Women’s section with 16. Grandmaster Yağız Kaan Erdoğmuş also won individual silver on board one, scoring 8/10 without a loss.
The team portraits capture a memorable moment from the tournament. HADITH Hotel celebrates Samarkand’s international spirit and the visitors who bring the city’s heritage to life.

indonesian-chess-team-hotel-kampoeng-ind.title: Indonesian Chess Contingent Welcomed at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia
indonesian-chess-team-hotel-kampoeng-ind.excerpt: Indonesia’s teams for the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand stayed at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia in the Imam Al Bukhari Complex.
indonesian-chess-team-hotel-kampoeng-ind.alt: Guests welcomed at the Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia reception, Samarkand
body: Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia welcomed Indonesia’s chess contingent as they prepared for the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand in 2026. Players arrived at reception with their luggage and accreditation, in a setting that felt close to home. The hotel, within the Imam Al Bukhari Memorial Complex, offered a familiar Indonesian character while the teams prepared for one of the world’s leading team chess championships, held this year in the historic Silk Road city of Samarkand.

Indonesia fielded two teams: Open and Women. The Open team comprised GM Susanto Megaranto, IM Arif Abdul Hafiz, IM Gilbert Elroy Tarigan, IM Satria Duta Cahaya, and IM Nayaka Budhidharma. The Women’s team included WIM Diajeng Theresa Singgih, WIM Laysa Latifah, WIM Chelsie Monica Sihite, WIM Shafira Devi Herfesa, and WIM Ummi Fisabilillah.

Staying at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia — one expression of Indonesian hospitality in the Imam Al Bukhari Memorial Complex — gave the national contingent a cultural setting they recognised while far from home. A comfortable place to rest and prepare between rounds allowed the players to focus on each stage of the Olympiad. Guests and supporters in Samarkand could follow Indonesia’s campaign knowing the athletes were lodged in a place that carries Indonesian character in the city.

uzbekistan-tourism-hotels-direct-flights.title: EBI Resources and Uzbekistan’s Tourism Committee Discuss Hotels and Direct Air Links
uzbekistan-tourism-hotels-direct-flights.excerpt: On 10 September 2026, the CEO met Tourism Committee chairman Abdulaziz Akkulov on hospitality investment and visitor flows from Indonesia.
uzbekistan-tourism-hotels-direct-flights.alt: Talks on Uzbekistan tourism, hotels, and connectivity
body: Indonesia–Uzbekistan tourism ties continue to deepen. On 10 September 2026, EBI Resources CEO Erslan G. Ibrahim met Abdulaziz Akkulov, chairman of Uzbekistan’s Tourism Committee, to discuss investment and cooperation — from Indonesian hotels and restaurants to the prospect of direct flights to Samarkand and Bukhara.

The talks also addressed how more Indonesian travellers might visit Uzbekistan. Projects discussed included Hadith Hotel at the Imam Bukhari complex in Samarkand and Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia. Both sides considered a familiarization tour for Indonesian travel-industry figures, to introduce Uzbekistan’s destinations — especially religious and cultural travel — at first hand.

Cooperation then turned to promotion and communications. Deputy chairman S. Tadjiev met Iwel Sastra to discuss introducing Uzbekistan to Indonesian audiences through media, influencers, events, concerts, and religious-tourism promotion. The Government of Uzbekistan is preparing a survey of Indonesian traveller interest and has proposed a press tour for Indonesian influencers. The EBI Resources delegation was also invited to the Tashkent International Tourism Fair (TITF-2026).

tourism-investment-hotel-operations-uzbe.title: EBI Resources Advances Tourism Investment and Hotel Operations in Uzbekistan
tourism-investment-hotel-operations-uzbe.excerpt: A strategic meeting with Uzbekistan’s National Tourism Committee focused on investment delivery and closer tourism ties.
tourism-investment-hotel-operations-uzbe.alt: Meeting on tourism investment and hotel operations in Uzbekistan
body: EBI Resources held a strategic meeting with Uzbekistan’s National Tourism Committee to advance tourism investment projects and to strengthen cooperation between Indonesia and Uzbekistan. CEO Erslan G. Ibrahim set out the group’s commitment to tourism connectivity, infrastructure in historic centres such as Bukhara and Samarkand, and national cultural programmes.

Uzbekistan’s tourism authorities welcomed the initiative and expressed support for an integrated, sustainable tourism agenda. To help investment proceed smoothly, the Tourism Committee appointed a team from its International Cooperation Division to accompany licensing, legal support, and official agency facilitation.

The cooperation also covers tourism promotion between the two countries through media in Jakarta, and a planned Indonesia–Uzbekistan Pavilion in Tashkent as a lasting platform for investment. Both sides hope the partnership will deepen and that Uzbekistan will remain a leading destination for travellers and investors from Indonesia.

gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.title: Gus Irfan Visits Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia at the Imam Bukhari Complex, Samarkand
gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.excerpt: Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia during an official programme in Samarkand.
gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.alt: Official visit at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, Samarkand
body: Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Mochamad Irfan Yusuf — known as Gus Irfan — visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia in the Imam Bukhari memorial complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The visit took place during his official programme in Samarkand, after accepting an invitation from the Governor of Samarkand, Adiz Muzaffarovich Boboev. During the visit, Gus Irfan joined a midday meal of Indonesian dishes prepared at the hotel.

Gus Irfan welcomed Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia as part of EBI Resources’ investment from Indonesia in Uzbekistan. The Indonesian-concept hotel is regarded as a way to introduce Indonesian cuisine, culture, and identity in a place that draws travellers and pilgrims from many countries. The visit also offered a first-hand look at facilities that carry an Indonesian atmosphere within the Imam Bukhari complex.

In addition to Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, Gus Irfan visited the Imam Bukhari memorial complex and paid respects at the shrine. He was accompanied by Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Siti Ruhaini Dzuhayatin. The programme formed part of his working visit to Samarkand and of closer ties between Indonesia and Uzbekistan.

hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.title: Hadith Hotel Holds Soft Opening in Samarkand
hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.excerpt: Hadith Hotel marked its soft opening at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex on Saturday, 5 September 2026.
hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.alt: Hadith Hotel soft opening in Samarkand
body: EBI Resources held the soft opening of Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Saturday, 5 September 2026. The hotel is a further step for Indonesian hospitality in Central Asia, a region with strong potential in tourism, hospitality, and pilgrimage travel.

The soft opening was attended by figures from Indonesia and Uzbekistan, including Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Mochamad Irfan Yusuf; Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Prof. Dr. Siti Ruhaini Dzuhayatin; and Indonesia’s Ambassador to Kazakhstan, M. Fadjroel Rachman. Their presence reflected closer Indonesia–Uzbekistan relations and the scope for economic and investment cooperation in the region.

Management of EBI Resources underlined that Hadith Hotel offers international-standard accommodation while carrying Indonesian hospitality onto a global stage. The hotel includes 114 rooms and suites, Indonesian dining, an Uzbek cuisine lounge, an indoor pool, spa, sauna, Turkish hammam, tennis, and a padel court. It is intended to support Samarkand’s international tourism and to strengthen EBI Resources’ presence abroad.

hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.title: Near the Imam Bukhari Shrine, Hadith Hotel Brings an Indonesian Touch to Samarkand
hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.excerpt: Hadith Hotel opened beside the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, combining Uzbek setting with international comfort.
hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.alt: Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand
body: Hadith Hotel held its soft opening at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Saturday, 5 September 2026. Less than a kilometre from the shrine of Imam Muhammad Al-Bukhari, the hotel — developed by EBI Resources — offers modern accommodation that brings together an Uzbek setting and international comfort.

Hadith Hotel has 114 rooms and suites, with occupancy for up to 250 guests. Five room types serve pilgrims, travellers, and VIP guests: 62 Standard Rooms, 23 Balcony Rooms, 18 Suites, 9 Junior Suites, and 2 President Suites. Its place within the Imam Al Bukhari precinct is well suited to visitors coming for pilgrimage and for Samarkand’s history and culture.

Beyond accommodation, Hadith Hotel offers Indonesian dining, an Uzbek cuisine lounge, an indoor pool, a fitness centre, spa, sauna, Turkish hammam, tennis, and a padel court. The hotel is intended to strengthen hospitality in Samarkand and to serve as a cultural bridge between Indonesia and Uzbekistan through travel and Nusantara hospitality.

ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.title: Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan Meets the CEO of EBI Resources on Tourism Cooperation
ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.excerpt: In Jakarta on 31 August 2026, the ambassador and the CEO discussed investment in Uzbekistan and the inauguration of Hadith Hotel.
ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.alt: Meeting on tourism cooperation and the Hadith Hotel inauguration
body: Jakarta, 31 August 2026 — The CEO of EBI Resources received Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan to discuss the next steps in the group’s investment in Uzbekistan. On that occasion the CEO invited the Ambassador to attend the inauguration of Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari memorial complex in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The two sides also discussed the potential for EBI Resources to expand its investment in Uzbekistan, and the importance of more Indonesian travellers visiting Uzbekistan for general tourism and pilgrimage.

The Ambassador welcomed the idea of more visitors travelling between Indonesia and Uzbekistan, which is expected to be supported by a planned direct flight between Jakarta and Tashkent in the near term. She expressed the hope that EBI Resources’ investment in Uzbekistan, together with that planned route, would strengthen tourism cooperation between the two countries.

Both sides also hoped that closer investment and socio-cultural ties would be matched by closer government-to-government cooperation, including high-level visits, to further strengthen bilateral relations between Indonesia and Uzbekistan.

wahdah-islamiyah-visits-ebi-resources.title: Wahdah Islamiyah Chairman Visits EBI Resources on Investment and Religious Tourism in Uzbekistan
wahdah-islamiyah-visits-ebi-resources.excerpt: Muhammad Zaitun Rasmin met the founder and leadership of EBI Resources to discuss cooperation in investment and pilgrimage travel.
wahdah-islamiyah-visits-ebi-resources.alt: Meeting at the EBI Resources office with the chairman of Wahdah Islamiyah
body: The chairman of Wahdah Islamiyah and head of ukhuwah at the Indonesian Ulema Council, Muhammad Zaitun Rasmin, visited the offices of EBI Resources. He was received by founder and CEO Erslan G. Ibrahim together with members of the board and the company’s advisors. The meeting was a courtesy call and an exchange of views on cooperation in investment and tourism.

Ustaz Zaitun Rasmin spoke of his visits to Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia and Hadith Hotel at the Imam Bukhari Complex in Samarkand — properties that form part of EBI Resources’ investment in Uzbekistan. He commended their facilities and service, and the comfort they offer travellers, especially Indonesian visitors to Islamic heritage sites in Uzbekistan.

The two sides also discussed the growing interest among Indonesians in religious tourism in Uzbekistan, and the scope for collaboration among businesses, institutions, and communities to strengthen tourism and investment links between Indonesia and Uzbekistan. The meeting closed with a shared meal and a commitment to future cooperation.

tabung-haji-chairman-hadith-hotel.title: Tabung Haji Malaysia Chairman Welcomes Talks on Religious Tourism in Uzbekistan
tabung-haji-chairman-hadith-hotel.excerpt: Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain recalled his stay at Hadith Hotel and discussed cooperation with EBI Resources in Kuala Lumpur.
tabung-haji-chairman-hadith-hotel.alt: Meeting with the chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji Malaysia
body: The chairman of Lembaga Tabung Haji Malaysia, Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, spoke warmly of his stay at Hadith Hotel in the Imam Bukhari memorial complex, Samarkand. He had lodged there while attending The First International Conference: Al-Jami’ al-Musnad al-Sahih: The Book of an Ummah. He had also visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia with Malaysia’s Minister of Religious Affairs, Dr. Zulkifli Hasan, and the Malaysian scholar Dr. Maza.

He shared that experience in a meeting with EBI Resources representatives Agus Ruhiat and Iwel Sastra at the Tabung Haji offices in Kuala Lumpur. The two sides discussed cooperation between TH Travel & Services and EBI Resources on religious tourism in Uzbekistan. Tan Sri noted that hotels in the Samarkand pilgrimage precinct are well placed to serve Malaysian travellers and congregational groups visiting Uzbekistan.

The meeting also touched on Uzbekistan’s growing promotion of religious tourism, especially in Samarkand and Tashkent. Both sides hoped that cooperation between TH Travel & Services and EBI Resources would become a working partnership — in travel, and as a mark of closer ties among Indonesia, Malaysia, and Muslim communities linking Southeast Asia with Uzbekistan.

tabung-haji-four-hotels-uzbekistan.title: EBI Resources Explores Hospitality Cooperation with Tabung Haji Malaysia
tabung-haji-four-hotels-uzbekistan.excerpt: In Kuala Lumpur, EBI Resources presented its Uzbekistan hospitality portfolio to Tabung Haji leadership.
tabung-haji-four-hotels-uzbekistan.alt: EBI Resources and Tabung Haji Malaysia discuss hospitality cooperation
body: EBI Resources visited the offices of Lembaga Tabung Haji Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur to explore cooperation in religious tourism. Representatives Agus Ruhiat and Iwel Sastra presented the group’s hospitality portfolio in Uzbekistan, including Hadith Hotel and Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia at the Imam Bukhari Complex in Samarkand.

The visit was received by Tabung Haji chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, who introduced the chairman of TH Travel & Services, Mohamed Izam bin Mohamed Yusof, and its CEO, YM Tengku Dato’ Badlishah Shukri bin Tengku Ibrahim. The discussion focused on travel and accommodation for Malaysian visitors to Uzbekistan.

Both sides considered Uzbekistan’s promotion of Islamic heritage destinations in Samarkand and Tashkent, and the possibility that EBI Resources hotels could serve Malaysian travellers — in particular pilgrims and guests visiting historic Islamic sites.

hadith-hotel-hosts-ministers-islamic-for.title: Hadith Hotel Hosts Ministerial Delegations from Seven Countries at the International Islamic Forum
hadith-hotel-hosts-ministers-islamic-for.excerpt: Hadith Hotel was official accommodation for senior delegates during the First International Islamic Forum in Uzbekistan, 7–11 July 2026.
hadith-hotel-hosts-ministers-islamic-for.alt: Hadith Hotel during the International Islamic Forum in Samarkand
body: The First International Islamic Forum, “Islamic Civilisation: The Path of Peace, Tolerance, and Enlightenment,” was held in Uzbekistan from 7 to 11 July 2026, with programmes in Tashkent, Samarkand, and Termez. Organised by Uzbekistan’s Centre of Islamic Civilisation together with ICESCO, the forum brought together more than 300 scholars, academics, researchers, and senior officials to discuss the contribution of Islamic civilisation to peace, tolerance, and learning.

Hadith Hotel, EBI Resources’ hotel in Samarkand, was among the official accommodation for high-level delegates. Ministers recorded as staying at the hotel included those of Awqaf of Syria; Culture of Palestine; Information and Culture of Afghanistan; Islamic Affairs and Awqaf of the Maldives; Religious Affairs of Malaysia; Higher Education and Scientific Research of Egypt; and National Heritage and Culture of Pakistan.

The forum formed part of Uzbekistan’s effort to host dialogue on Islamic civilisation and to present the scholarly heritage of Central Asia. Hosting ministerial delegations at Hadith Hotel also marked Indonesian hospitality investment in Uzbekistan and the hotel’s role in a major international programme in Central Asia.

hadith-hotel-official-accommodation-isla.title: Hadith Hotel Named Official Accommodation for the International Islamic Forum in Uzbekistan
hadith-hotel-official-accommodation-isla.excerpt: The five-star hotel at the Imam Bukhari Complex hosted delegates and forum sessions attended by scholars from many regions.
hadith-hotel-official-accommodation-isla.alt: Hadith Hotel at the Imam Bukhari Complex during the international forum
body: Hadith Hotel, at the Imam Bukhari memorial complex in Samarkand, was named official accommodation for delegates to the First International Islamic Forum, held in Uzbekistan from 7 to 11 July 2026. The five-star hotel, part of EBI Resources, also hosted forum meetings attended by more than 300 scholars, researchers, religious figures, and specialists from the Middle East to Europe.

The forum, “Islamic Civilisation: The Path of Peace, Tolerance, and Enlightenment,” was organised by Uzbekistan’s Centre of Islamic Civilisation and ICESCO. Over five days, programmes in Tashkent, Samarkand, and Termez included high-level plenaries, an international scholarly conference, exhibitions of manuscripts and Islamic calligraphy, and documentary screenings. The agenda also highlighted the contribution of Central Asian scholars — among them Imam Bukhari, Imam Maturidi, Imam Tirmidhi, and Alisher Navoi — to Islamic learning and civilisational dialogue.

For EBI Resources, the hotel’s role as official accommodation and a venue for the forum was a further step in hospitality tied to heritage and religious travel. The appointment also underlined Hadith Hotel’s standing as a five-star property in the Imam Bukhari precinct and the place of Indonesian investment in religious tourism and cultural diplomacy in Central Asia.

muzani-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesia.title: After Visiting the Imam Bukhari Shrine, Ahmad Muzani Tours Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia
muzani-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesia.excerpt: The Speaker of Indonesia’s People’s Consultative Assembly visited the hotel after a pilgrimage to the shrine in Samarkand on 3 July.
muzani-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesia.alt: Ahmad Muzani and delegation at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, Samarkand
body: The Speaker of Indonesia’s People’s Consultative Assembly (MPR), Ahmad Muzani, together with a delegation of MPR members, pesantren leaders, ulama, and figures from Islamic organisations, visited the shrine of Imam Bukhari in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Friday, 3 July 2026. The visit formed part of a programme to deepen Indonesia–Uzbekistan relations and the long-standing historical and religious ties between the two nations.

After the pilgrimage, Ahmad Muzani and the delegation continued to Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, within the Imam Bukhari memorial complex. The three-star hotel is part of EBI Resources’ investment from Indonesia in Uzbekistan, and is intended to support Indonesian travellers and pilgrims visiting Samarkand.

The guests were served a midday meal at the hotel. Ahmad Muzani commended the Indonesian dishes offered in a religious-tourism setting in Uzbekistan, and the hotel’s Indonesian character, which he said gave comfort to guests — especially Indonesians visiting the shrine of Imam Bukhari.

kampoeng-indonesia-uzbekistan-national-c.title: Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia Receives Uzbekistan’s National Tourism Standard Certificate
kampoeng-indonesia-uzbekistan-national-c.excerpt: The hotel was awarded a national certificate of conformity for accommodation services, valid through 19 June 2031.
kampoeng-indonesia-uzbekistan-national-c.alt: National tourism certificate presentation for Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia
body: Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia in Samarkand has received a Muvofiqlik Sertifikati — a certificate of conformity — from the national certification system of the Republic of Uzbekistan. It was issued by the Tourism Services Certification Centre under Uzbekistan’s Tourism Committee, confirming that the hotel meets the country’s accommodation-service standards. The certificate is registered as UZ.SMT.02.0003.018630 and is valid until 19 June 2031.

The hotel was found to meet O‘z DSt 3220:2023 for hotel services. The certification confirms that operations and service align with standards set by the Government of Uzbekistan. Periodic inspection will continue during the certificate’s term so that service quality remains consistent with those requirements.

The award reflects Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia’s commitment to quality hospitality for domestic and international guests. With an Indonesian character in the heart of Samarkand, the hotel is intended as a considered choice for business travellers, visitors, and guests in Uzbekistan — and as a mark of Indonesian investment in the country’s tourism sector.

trade-vice-minister-visits-kampoeng-indo.title: Indonesia’s Vice Minister of Trade Visits Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia
trade-vice-minister-visits-kampoeng-indo.excerpt: Dyah Roro Esti Widya Putri visited the Samarkand hotel on 19 June and discussed export and hospitality cooperation.
trade-vice-minister-visits-kampoeng-indo.alt: Indonesia’s Vice Minister of Trade at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia
body: Indonesia’s Vice Minister of Trade, Dyah Roro Esti Widya Putri, visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on 19 June 2026. She was accompanied by the secretary of the Directorate General of International Trade Negotiation, Danang Prasta Danial, and Indonesia’s trade attaché posted in New Delhi.

The Vice Minister commended EBI Resources’ expansion in Uzbekistan through Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia. She also noted two further hotels — a three-star and a five-star property — then planned for inauguration in September 2026.

The Ministry of Trade expressed its support for strengthening the business setting in which EBI Resources operates in Uzbekistan. One focus is greater export of Indonesian goods, especially for hotels, restaurants, and cafés, into the Uzbek market, together with faster high-level talks on a free-trade arrangement between Indonesia and Uzbekistan, then expected to take place in Samarkand.
